summary: Yosemite National Park is a breathtaking wilderness featuring iconic granite cliffs, cascading waterfalls, giant sequoias, and pristine alpine meadows that attract photographers and adventurers worldwide. With over 1,200 square miles of stunning landscapes and world-class outdoor activities, it's one of America's most visited and photographed national parks.

restaurants.name: Degnan's Kitchen
restaurants.description: Casual dining spot in Yosemite Village offering sandwiches, salads, and wraps with fresh ingredients. Quick service perfect for grabbing lunch before hitting the trails.

restaurants.name: Tuolumne Meadows Grill
restaurants.description: Seasonal outdoor grill serving burgers, hot dogs, and simple fare in a scenic high-altitude setting. Great for a casual meal with mountain views.

restaurants.name: Mountain Room Restaurant
restaurants.description: Contemporary dining with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Yosemite Falls, offering American cuisine with seasonal menus. Reservations highly recommended.

restaurants.name: Curry Village Pizza Patio
restaurants.description: Casual pizzeria with outdoor seating offering wood-fired pizzas and simple Italian fare. Popular gathering spot for families and hikers.

restaurants.name: The Majestic Yosemite Hotel Restaurant
restaurants.description: Elegant dining in a historic 1927 hotel featuring classic American cuisine and an extensive wine list with fine service and elegant ambiance.

restaurants.name: Wawona Hotel Dining Room
restaurants.description: Classic hotel restaurant with family-style dining and a fireplace, serving comfort food and regional specialties in a historic setting.

restaurants.name: Ahwahnee Lounge
restaurants.description: Historic lounge offering light fare, cocktails, and appetizers in an architecturally stunning room with natural stone and massive windows.

restaurants.name: White Wolf Lodge Dining
restaurants.description: Seasonal rustic dining experience with family-style service offering hearty American meals in an intimate mountain lodge setting.

restaurants.name: Four Mile Trail Picnic Spot
restaurants.description: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at scenic overlooks along popular hiking trails throughout the park. DIY dining with unbeatable views.

restaurants.name: Glacier Point Snack Stand
restaurants.description: Seasonal outdoor snack bar serving light refreshments, ice cream, and cold beverages at one of the park's most scenic viewpoints.

restaurants.name: Yosemite Village Store Café
restaurants.description: Convenient café in the village offering coffee, pastries, and sandwiches for quick breakfast or lunch before adventures.

restaurants.name: Mono Lake Visitor Center Café
restaurants.description: Simple regional café near Mono Lake serving local favorites and providing insight into the Eastern Sierra ecosystem.

activities.name: Mist Trail Hike
activities.description: Popular 5.5-mile round trip hike to Vernal Fall with stunning views and refreshing mist from the waterfall. Steep sections with cables provide an exhilarating challenge.

activities.name: Valley Loop Trail
activities.description: Scenic 7.2-mile mostly flat trail circling Yosemite Valley with views of El Capitan, Bridalveil Fall, and Half Dome. Accessible for most fitness levels.

activities.name: Half Dome Cable Route
activities.description: Challenging 16-17 mile round trip climb to Half Dome's summit using iconic steel cables and granite slabs. Requires permits and extreme fitness.

activities.name: Glacier Point Road Scenic Drive
activities.description: Stunning 20-mile drive offering breathtaking panoramic views of Half Dome, Yosemite Valley, and the High Sierra. Open seasonally, spectacular at sunrise and sunset.

activities.name: Mirror Lake Loop
activities.description: Peaceful 5-mile loop trail around a reflective alpine lake with views of Half Dome and surrounding cliffs. Best in spring and early summer when water levels are high.

activities.name: Bridalveil Fall Walk
activities.description: Easy 0.5-mile paved trail to the base of this iconic 620-foot waterfall, often framed by rainbows. One of the most accessible waterfalls in the park.

activities.name: Tuolumne Meadows Exploration
activities.description: High-altitude meadows with numerous hiking options, wildflower blooms, and granite peaks. Popular base for backcountry hiking and day trips.

activities.name: Rock Climbing and Bouldering
activities.description: World-class climbing destination with routes for all skill levels on iconic granite formations. Requires permits and proper equipment or guided services.

activities.name: Stargazing at Badger Pass
activities.description: Experience some of the darkest skies in California with exceptional views of the Milky Way and constellations. Best in clear, moonless nights.

activities.name: Mariposa Grove Giant Sequoia Walk
activities.description: Guided or self-guided walks through groves of massive ancient sequoias, the largest trees on Earth. Multiple trail options from 1 to 6 miles.

activities.name: Backcountry Camping and Wilderness Trips
activities.description: Multi-day backpacking expeditions into pristine wilderness areas with alpine lakes and high passes. Requires permits and self-sufficiency.

activities.name: Yosemite Museum and Village Exploration
activities.description: Learn about Yosemite's natural and human history through exhibits, galleries, and cultural sites. Family-friendly indoor activity on rainy days.

spots.name: El Capitan
spots.description: Massive 3,000-foot granite monolith best photographed from the valley floor at sunrise with dramatic side lighting.

spots.name: Half Dome from Glacier Point
spots.description: Iconic granite peak framed perfectly from this high-altitude viewpoint, especially stunning during sunset with alpenglow.

spots.name: Bridalveil Fall
spots.description: Ethereal 620-foot waterfall with mist and often rainbow, captured best with wide-angle lens during peak flow season.

spots.name: Mirror Lake Reflection
spots.description: Perfect mirror reflections of Half Dome and surrounding peaks in calm morning waters, best in spring and early summer.
spots.bestTime: Early morning before wind ripples the water

spots.name: Four Mile Trail Overlooks
spots.description: Multiple stunning vistas of Yosemite Valley from different angles with varied lighting throughout the day.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour near sunrise or sunset

spots.name: Mariposa Grove Giant Sequoias
spots.description: Ancient massive trees creating dramatic vertical compositions with filtered light through the canopy.
spots.bestTime: Overcast days or morning light filtering through trees

spots.name: Tunnel View
spots.description: Classic postcard view of El Capitan, Bridalveil Fall, and Half Dome framed by granite cliffs.

spots.name: Vernal Fall from Mist Trail
spots.description: Powerful 317-foot waterfall photographed through mist and spray, creating ethereal soft-focus effects.
spots.bestTime: Midday when sun is high and creates rainbow in mist

spots.name: Mono Lake and Eastern Sierra
spots.description: Unique landscape with tufa towers and alkaline lake reflecting dramatic mountain peaks in eastern Yosemite region.
spots.bestTime: Sunrise and sunset for rich colors

spots.name: Yosemite Falls Moonlit Night
spots.description: Iconic 2,425-foot waterfall illuminated by moonlight during full moon nights creating ethereal nocturnal compositions.
spots.bestTime: Full moon nights with clear skies

lensRecommendations: 16-35mm wide-angle for expansive landscape and dramatic valley compositions
70-200mm telephoto for compressing distant peaks and isolating waterfall details
24-105mm versatile zoom for variety of compositions from wide valleys to tighter framing
50mm prime for intimate tree and detail photography in Mariposa Grove
photography.goldenHourNotes: Yosemite's granite cliffs provide exceptional golden hour lighting from multiple viewpoints. Early morning light from Glacier Point bathes the valley in warm tones while evening light from Valley View creates dramatic side-lighting on El Capitan. The high elevation extends golden hour duration compared to lower elevations.

weather.seasonality: Summer (June-August) offers warm, dry weather perfect for hiking and camping, though crowds are heaviest. Spring and fall provide mild temperatures with fewer visitors and stunning wildflowers or fall colors, while winter brings snow and limited access to high-elevation areas.
weather.summary: Yosemite experiences four distinct seasons with winter bringing heavy snow to valley floors and road closures above. Summer is warm and mostly dry with temperatures ranging 15-28°C, making it ideal for outdoor activities despite peak crowds.

hotels.name: Yosemite Valley Lodge
hotels.description: Basic motel-style rooms in the valley offering convenient access to major attractions and dining with functional amenities and valley views from some rooms.

hotels.name: The Majestic Yosemite Hotel
hotels.description: Historic 1927 hotel with elegant Art Deco architecture, fine dining, and fireplace lounges offering classic Yosemite hospitality with modern amenities and valley proximity.

hotels.name: Ahwahnee Hotel
hotels.description: Iconic luxury resort with architectural grandeur, world-class dining, spa facilities, and dramatic valley views representing the ultimate Yosemite experience with impeccable service.
